record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: For generalized tiling billiards in the cyclic pentagonal tilings obtained by replacing a square lattice with congruent cyclic pentagons formed from a shifted lattice point, determine the generic behavior of trajectories.

evidence.quote: generic behavior is not yet known

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following construction of a "cyclic pentagonal tiling" of the plane. Start with the standard square lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ and choose a point $p$ in the interior of the unit square $[0,1]^2$ that is not its center. For each unit square cell of the lattice, place a translated copy of $p$ inside it; together with the four corners of that cell, these five points form a (generically) cyclic pentagon (i.e., a pentagon whose vertices lie on a common circle). Replacing each square by the corresponding congruent cyclic pentagon yields an arrangement of congruent cyclic pentagons that covers the plane (with possible overlaps), called a cyclic pentagonal tiling.

A generalized tiling billiard trajectory in such an arrangement is defined as follows: a particle moves in straight line segments inside a pentagonal cell; whenever it crosses an edge $e$ of a pentagon, it is refracted by reflecting its direction across $e$ (equivalently, the trajectory is continued into the centrally symmetric copy of the pentagon glued along $e$), and motion continues in straight lines, refracting at each subsequent edge crossing.

Determine the generic dynamical behavior of trajectories of this generalized tiling billiard system in cyclic pentagonal tilings: for a generic choice of the shifted lattice point $p$ and a generic initial condition (starting point and direction), describe the long-term behavior of the trajectory (e.g., whether it is bounded, escapes to infinity, follows an asymptotic direction, has linear or sublinear deviations, is periodic, etc.).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Jay, "Deviations for generalized tiling billiards in cyclic polygons", arXiv:2402.15765, IMRN 2025) studies generalized tiling billiards in cyclic N-gons with N ≥ 5, including pentagonal cases. It exhibits an open set of trajectories that deviate sublinearly from their asymptotic direction (a behavior strikingly different from triangular and quadrilateral tilings, where almost every trajectory stays bounded distance from a line) and establishes deviation rates in generic and certain non-generic cases. This provides substantial progress but does not yet give a complete description of the generic behavior of trajectories in the cyclic pentagonal tilings, so the problem appears partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Deviations for generalized tiling billiards in cyclic polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Exhibits an open set of generalized tiling billiard trajectories in cyclic N-gons (N ≥ 5) that deviate sublinearly from their asymptotic direction, and establishes the rate of deviations in generic and some non-generic cases.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on generic behavior in cyclic pentagonal (and more general cyclic N-gon, N ≥ 5) tiling billiards.

status_evidence.title: Deviations for Generalized Tiling Billiards in Cyclic Polygons, IMRN 2025
status_evidence.snippet: Published version studying deviation behavior of generalized tiling billiards in cyclic polygons, showing behavior for N ≥ 5 differs significantly from N = 3, 4.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results address—but do not fully resolve—the generic behavior question in cyclic pentagonal tilings.
